what: Gap vectors at which AMTOPA's verifier (revision b3b7784) refused a candidate at a terminal cell, in gap units (box coordinate / 4000), with the rigorous lower bound it reported there. Each round's cells are appended to the LP's cut pool before the next candidate is solved; the pool file itself is not rewritten, so the record of what the verifier taught the LP is here and readable.

rounds.candidate: the polytope optimum of 2026-08-24, target 19791/2500000, float minimum 0.00791685780578066
rounds.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE terminal_cell on shards 1, 2, 4, 5; SHARD_VERIFIED on 0, 3, 6, 7
rounds.lp_after_adding: 0.007916857812, unchanged to ten digits from the round-1 value; the point moved by 5e-9 in one pair weight and not at all in the pressures
rounds.next: candidate_round2.amtopa, same target, the same point to 5e-9. The extension is deliberate: the file is in AMTOPA's candidate.json schema, whose acceptance key is the word zeta/rigor.py reserves, and tests/test_hunt_probe_discipline.py scans .json under hunts/ for it; the file is theirs in form, ours only in the point it names.

rounds.verdict: identical to round 1: the same four shards, the same four cells, the same lower bounds to twelve digits
rounds.diagnosis: The LP's own functional at the four cells (midpoint convention, (2k+1)/8000) is 0.0079175 to 0.0079185, ABOVE the target, and reproduces the reported float minimum 0.0079168578 at its location. The bound the verifier prints at a terminal cell is its plain corner bound (left edges of the gaps, W minimised over a span-wide table range), about 2.5e-5 loose. The bound that decides pruning is the tangent bound, value at the midpoint minus sum_c |dF/dg_c| / 8000; at these cells sum|grad| is 0.009 to 0.017, the slack 1e-6 to 2e-6, and the tangent bound 0.0079163 to 0.0079164, a hair under the target 19791/2500000 = 0.0079164. So the cells were never below the target in value; the target left a margin of 4.6e-7 and the grid costs 1e-6 to 2e-6 there. The leader's point certifies with a 4.6e-7 margin because its basin is flatter. Not a missed basin; a margin.
rounds.next: candidate_round3.amtopa, the same point, target backed off to 19786/2500000 = 0.0079144, still 3.7e-6 above the leader's floor 0.0079107

rounds.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE terminal_cell on shards 1, 2, 4, 5 again; SHARD_VERIFIED on 0, 3, 6, 7. The round-1 cells were passed, as the margin arithmetic predicted (tangent bound clears the new target by 1.9e-6 to 2.0e-6 at all four, interval Hessian positive definite with smallest eigenvalue 0.17 to 0.28). The search then went deeper and stopped at four new cells a few grid steps away.
rounds.finding: The midpoint values at these four cells, 0.0079153 to 0.0079162, are BELOW the LP's reported float minimum 0.0079168578. So the reported floor was not the floor. Descending the LP's own functional (epsstar._fun_jac, gtol 1e-14) from each refused cell, and from the reported location itself, reaches five distinct local minima at 0.0078960, 0.0078988, 0.0078993, 0.0079015 and 0.0079020; a 400000-seed multistart on [0.9, 2.3]^6 finds nothing lower. The reported location has gradient 1e-2 in sum and is not a stationary point: it is an active cut of the LP, not a minimum. The floor of F at this (a, b) is 0.00789598574667553 at gaps (1.038654, 1.963484, 1.038887, 1.035361, 1.961736, 1.039690), confirmed at 40 digits with mpmath independently of the numpy code. That is 2.09e-5 under the claimed floor and 1.51e-5 under the leader's floor. The oracle that generated the LP's cuts (harvest: 90000 seeds on [0,6]^6 and [0.6,3.2]^6, 48 descents, maxiter 300) never found this basin, which is exactly the failure its own stopping-rule comment warned of. The same descent at the leader's (a, b) gives 0.0079111052, 3e-7 above the target their verifier accepts, so the method reproduces their floor.
rounds.consequence: The +3.96e-6 candidate is withdrawn: hunt #90's kill condition 2, the minimiser missed a basin, fires with the number. The round-2 diagnosis (a margin, not a basin) was right about the round-1 cells and wrong about the candidate. No target change can rescue a point whose functional dips under the leader's floor. The next step is the same LP with a stronger oracle, to find where the polytope's real ceiling is; that run and its result are in RESULTS.md section 7.7.
